covers.quote: Use forward slashes:
in some shortened forms
in mathematical expressions
to present lines of poetry in body text
instead of ‘per’, ‘an’ or ‘a’ when abbreviating units of measurement
in web addresses
in dates if you can’t write them out – for example, in tables
in some place names.

rules.quote: Limit the forward slash to specific uses
rules.specification: The page does not exhaustively identify the shortened forms or place names that qualify, or define when a date cannot be written out. Treat this as a residual restriction on slash uses; cite the more specific rules below when they apply.
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash used outside the listed contexts: conventional shortened forms, mathematical expressions, poetry line breaks in body text, abbreviated measurement units, web addresses, dates that cannot be written out, and recognised place names.
when: The listed contexts permit slashes; they do not require slashes in every expression within those contexts.
Slashes in dates are permitted when the dates cannot be written out, for example in tables.
Use the specific measurement, financial-year, alternatives, ‘and/or’ and word-joining checks instead when they apply.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the permitted contexts together; G-3 prevents turning each permission into a separate requirement, and the one-finding test gives specific prohibitions precedence.

covers.quote: There is no need to include a space on either side of a forward slash.
The exceptions are for:
official dual place names
lines of poetry in body text

rules.quote: Don’t add spaces around most forward slashes
rules.violation_condition: A space immediately before or after a forward slash outside the stated exceptions.
when: Do not apply this prohibition to official dual place names.
Do not apply this prohibition to slashes marking poetry line breaks in body text.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the exceptions with the no-space check; the explicit requirement for poetry spacing produces a different, missing-space finding.

rules.quote: lines of poetry in body text – use forward slashes with spaces around them to show the line breaks.
rules.violation_condition: A slash marking a poetry line break in body text without a separating space on one or both sides.
when: When a forward slash represents a poetry line break in body text.
rules.why: The one-finding test separates missing required poetry spacing from the general prohibition on extra spaces.

covers.quote: If you must, include the slash before the line break so that the reader anticipates it as they read the next line.

rules.quote: As far as possible, avoid using forward slashes either side of a line break.
rules.specification: The page does not define when adjacency to a line break is unavoidable. Assessing this qualification requires print-layout information.
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash directly beside an avoidable print line break, or a slash placed after the line break when the split is unavoidable.
when: For print layouts.
If the slash must be beside a line break, put it before the break rather than at the start of the next line.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the fallback placement condition with the line-break restriction rather than creating overlapping findings.

covers.quote: instead of ‘per’, ‘an’ or ‘a’ when abbreviating units of measurement

rules.quote: Write shortened units of measurement with a forward slash
rules.violation_condition: A measurement rate expressed using shortened unit names but lacking the forward slash representing ‘per’, ‘an’ or ‘a’.
when: When shortened units express a rate or division relationship.
A single abbreviated unit does not require a slash merely because it is abbreviated.
rules.why: The one-finding test separates a missing slash in abbreviated rates from a prohibited slash with spelt-out units.

rules.quote: Don’t use forward slashes when spelling out units of measurement.
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash used as the separator in a measurement rate whose unit names are spelt out.
when: When unit names are spelt out rather than shortened.
rules.why: This is not a restatement of the heading: it prohibits a present slash, while the heading requires a missing one; E-2 attaches the spelt-out-unit examples here.

covers.quote: Don’t use a forward slash as a replacement for an en dash in financial years.

rules.quote: Use an en dash for financial years, not a slash
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash separating the years in a financial-year expression.
when: When the expression denotes a financial year.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and its body restatement into one financial-year separator check.

covers.quote: When showing alternatives, use ‘or’ instead of a forward slash.

rules.quote: Write ‘or’ instead of a slash for alternatives
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash used between alternatives in place of the word ‘or’.
when: When the slash represents a choice between alternatives.
Use the separate explicit prohibition for the fixed form ‘and/or’.
rules.why: G-4 merges the heading and restatement; the one-finding test avoids also reporting ‘and/or’ under this general check.

covers.quote: Rewrite the sentence to make the meaning clear.

rules.why: This is a distinct fixed-form prohibition; G-5 treats the rewriting instruction as remediation rather than another finding.

covers.quote: Don’t join words with a slash
Instead, either use an en dash or reword the sentence.

rules.quote: Don’t use a forward slash between words that retain their separate identities.
rules.specification: Interpret ‘retain their separate identities’ as paired terms expressing a relationship, such as the endpoints of a flight. Do not extend the broad heading to permitted uses such as web addresses, conventional shortened forms, measurement rates or official dual place names.
rules.violation_condition: A forward slash joining distinct words to express a relationship or connection, rather than an alternative or another permitted slash use.
when: When joining distinct words to express a connection rather than offering alternatives.
rules.why: G-4 selects the qualified body sentence over the broader heading; the alternative treatments remedy the same finding.
